anomalies.observed: On sheet 1, T5 (AO3400A) has its gate on G_ATO. That net is connected to T4's collector and pulled down to GND through R12 (10 kΩ); T4's emitter is also grounded. There is no pull-up or other path to drive the gate high.
anomalies.expected: The ATO low-side MOSFET gate must be able to rise sufficiently above its source to turn T5 on, while the control circuitry can pull it low to turn it off.

evidence.quote: ATO Valve: T5 AO3400A gate on G_ATO; R12 10k from G_ATO to GND; T4 BT3904 emitter to GND (sheet 1, page 1).
The board automates “Automatic Top-Off (ATO)” and uses an “ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch” (page 1).

anomalies.impact: The ATO MOSFET gate is held low, so the valve driver cannot switch on; automatic top-off will not actuate the solenoid.

parsed.summary: The ATO MOSFET gate is pulled to ground and its NPN driver can only sink current, leaving no way to raise the gate. The valve therefore cannot be switched on.
